Explicit calendarId requests resolve the named CalendarList entry directly. The browser demo retains its 24-calendar bound. CalendarList read permission remains required.
Read-only provider operation. This does not change calendar subscriptions or the bar.

timeZone.description: Optional window display zone; default is the selected calendar's time_zone. Day boundaries preserve daylight-saving changes.

commands.summary: Prepare and durably save one ordinary organizer event creation or conditional edit for review.

expectedEtag.description: Required for editing: exact event.etag from calendar.event. Omit eventId and expectedEtag for a new event.

sendUpdates.description: Explicit reviewed guest notification choice. all is mandatory when adding guests; use all when rescheduling a meeting so participants receive updates.

notes: No provider mutation occurs during review. Inspect the returned account, calendarName/calendarId, action, event, resolved time points, previous event and sendUpdates before applying its exact reviewHash.

Uses existing Calendar event-write OAuth permissions and calendar ACLs. Organizer-owned normal events and exact recurring occurrences can be edited. Attendee copies, locked/private copies and recurring series are refused.
Create uses a stable client event ID and the durable journal. Pending unknown creates block new creates in the same target calendar until reconciled; edit uses fresh ETag and If-Match.
DST gaps are refused. DST folds require explicit endpoint offsets or offset-bearing RFC3339 matching the named zone. All-day end is exclusive.

Meet creation requires supports_meet from calendar.list. Calendar save can succeed while conference_status is pending or failure: refresh calendar.event to inspect the generated join_url without recreating the event.

Attendee and conference arrays remain untouched when omitted. Adding guests requires sendUpdates all. Existing attendees retain their provider attributes/RSVP states. No third-party meeting API or extra OAuth scope is needed for a pasted join URL.

For edits, omitted or null description/location preserve existing exact values; explicit empty strings clear them. Omitted or null attendees preserve the complete list. Existing HTML notes remain byte-exact and read-only.

commands.summary: Apply one exact saved event review (create, edit, delete or response), dispatching at most once.

dryRun.description: true runs the same fresh checks as apply (saved review, current ETag, permissions, pending operations) and returns state not_sent with wouldSend {action, method, eventId, ifMatch, sendUpdates}. Nothing is saved, claimed or sent. An operation already recorded under this ID is reported instead.

notes: Use the exact saved calendar.event-review, calendar.event-delete-review or calendar.event-respond-review result. Caller-supplied draft, request or ETag overrides are refused. Invitation-import reviews cannot be applied through this command.

After a durable unknown claim, the provider write is dispatched once with no automatic retries. Inspect state applied/rejected/unknown even if the outer result envelope is ok; one-shot exit status is 6 for unknown and 3 for rejected.
Unknown results must use calendar.event-reconcile; do not retry under another operationId. Read-only reconciliation never resends invitations, cancellations or responses.

commands.summary: Resolve an unknown event write (create, edit, delete or response) by reading its exact provider event ID without resending it.
notes: Loads the exact saved event review (create, edit, delete or response) and durable journal. A delete is proven by the exact event being cancelled; a response by the private markers together with the reviewed answer. Applied proof requires the bound account/calendar/event ID and immutable private operation/source markers, even after later content changes or cancellation. A missing event remains unknown and can offer explicit identical-request retry; an unchanged edit ETag also remains uncertain.
Performs only reads. Never creates a second event, repeats a Meet request or resends attendee notifications.

commands.summary: Review deleting one existing event (or its whole recurring series) and save the exact conditional DELETE; nothing is deleted yet.

expectedEtag.description: Exact etag of eventId as you last read it (calendar.event, calendar.agenda or a dryRun review). Required unless dryRun:true; a changed event fails CalendarReviewStale.

scope.description: event deletes eventId only (one occurrence when it belongs to a series). series deletes every event of the recurring series and binds the series master's own ETag. This-and-following is not supported.

sendUpdates.description: all emails the guests a cancellation; only for an event this calendar organizes that has guests. none sends no email. Attendee copies always use none.

dryRun.description: true reads and checks only: no review is saved, so the reply has no reviewHash. It returns the role, guests, consequence and options (series, notify, thisAndFollowing) for choosing the real review.

notes: Returns action delete_event, role organizer|attendee|copy, scope, sendUpdates, eventId/expectedEtag, targetEventId/targetEtag (the If-Match version), summary, start, end, recurring, guestCount, organizer, consequence and reviewHash. Inspect consequence before calendar.event-apply with the same operationId and reviewHash.

role attendee or copy: only this calendar's copy is removed and Omagma sends no email; the organizer's event stays for the other guests. To tell the organizer you will not attend, use calendar.event-respond-review with response declined instead.

Refused with a stable code: CalendarReadOnly, CalendarWritePermissionRequired, CalendarEventLocked, CalendarPrivateCopy, CalendarSpecialEvent, CalendarEventCancelled, CalendarSeriesScopeRequired (eventId is a series master), CalendarNotRecurring, CalendarNotificationUnavailable, CalendarReviewStale, CalendarOperationPending.

Apply, reconcile, retry and archive use calendar.event-apply, calendar.event-reconcile, calendar.event-retry and calendar.event-abandon. A deletion is proven when Google reports the event cancelled; a missing event stays unknown. No undo is offered.

commands.summary: Review accepting, tentatively accepting or declining an event this calendar is invited to, and save the exact conditional response; nothing is sent yet.

expectedEtag.description: Exact etag of eventId as you last read it. Required unless dryRun:true; a changed event fails CalendarReviewStale.

scope.description: event answers eventId only (one occurrence when it belongs to a series). series answers the whole recurring series; occurrences answered separately may keep their own answer. This-and-following is not supported.

response.description: The answer. Required unless dryRun:true; a dry run without it returns the current previousResponse. The current answer is refused as CalendarResponseUnchanged.

sendUpdates.description: all asks Google to email your answer to the organizer. none sends no email; an organizer using Google Calendar still sees the answer on the shared event.

dryRun.description: true reads and checks only: no review is saved and the reply has no reviewHash.

notes: Only this calendar's own attendee entry changes (Google's attendeesOmitted response form) with private receipt markers; other guests, organizer fields and shared properties are not sent. No mail is composed by Omagma.

Refused with a stable code: CalendarOrganizerCannotRespond (this calendar organizes the event), NotAnAttendee, CalendarAttendeesOmitted, CalendarRespondOtherAttendee (another person's calendar), CalendarPrivateCopy (answer from the invitation mail with invitation.reply), CalendarEventLocked, CalendarReadOnly, CalendarWritePermissionRequired, CalendarResponseUnchanged.
Apply with calendar.event-apply. A response is proven by the reviewed answer plus this operation's markers on the exact event; otherwise it stays unknown until calendar.event-reconcile.

commands.summary: Open Google Calendar in this account’s configured Chrome profile.
notes: Without calendarId opens the account calendar; with calendarId selects an exact calendar from the account’s available calendars. Profile launch is explicit and uses the existing configured account profile. Returns opened, fixture, url, profile and cached/stale metadata.

commands.summary: Open an exact Calendar event in this account’s configured Chrome profile.
notes: Reads the exact account/calendar/event and validates its Google Calendar htmlLink before launching the account’s configured Chrome profile. Returns opened, fixture, url, profile and cached/stale metadata.

commands.summary: Explicitly retry an uncertain identical saved event request (edit, delete or response) once for this attempt token.
notes: Read event-reconcile first; retry only when retryPossible is true and the user confirms the identical request. Returned nextAttempt is a durable single-use send token; duplicate tokens cannot dispatch again.
Uses the original deterministic event ID, exact request body, Meet request ID and conditional edit ETag. No automatic retry. 404 and unchanged ETag remain uncertain.
An uncertain prior dispatch may still complete. Result state is applied, rejected, unknown or archived. When a previous dispatch is uncertain, later refusals alone cannot prove rejection.

commands.summary: Explicitly archive an uncertain event write (create, edit, delete or response) locally.
notes: Requires explicit user confirmation. Returns state archived, releases the pending guard and never sends any provider request.
The event may still appear in Calendar. Archived does not mean unsent or rejected. The saved form cannot be applied again.
The current local grant must retain mail-read and one of the Calendar capability alternatives; this check reads grant metadata without opening credentials.

commands.summary: Resume a saved uncertain Calendar write by operation ID, or the one that blocks changes to an event (its own, its series', or for a series an occurrence's).

eventId.description: Omit for pending creation; otherwise the event whose blocking write to find.

seriesEventId.description: The event's recurring_event_id from calendar.agenda or calendar.event ("" when it does not repeat). Without it the event is read once to learn its series. Alone (without eventId) it finds the writes on that series; "" alone is invalid.

operationId.description: Exact lookup, e.g. the blockingOperationId of a CalendarOperationPending refusal.

notes: Returns {pending:null|{review,relation,state,attempt,nextAttempt,retryPossible,recoveryReason},seriesChecked}. Review is the complete review result; relation is operation, creation, event (a write to this event or its whole series) or series (a write to another occurrence, which blocks a series action here). An invitation's own unknown update is reported as blockedBy {kind:invitation,operationId,reviewHash,uid,eventId,summary,previous,check,stopTracking}: calendar.event-reconcile with that operationId and reviewHash checks it with reads only; calendar.event-abandon stops tracking it after explicit confirmation.

Series membership is the provider's recurringEventId (seriesEventId or one events.get), never guessed from ID text; seriesChecked:false with readError means the event could not be read, so only writes to the exact event were checked. With operationId, seriesEventId, or no eventId it reads only local state, without provider traffic or credentials. Exact selected account/calendar binding is checked.
The current local grant must retain mail-read and one of the Calendar capability alternatives; this check reads grant metadata without opening credentials.

commands.summary: Review a new event with a Google Meet link and automatic AI notes + transcript. Reads only and saves a local review.

sendUpdates.description: Explicit reviewed guest notification choice. all is mandatory when adding guests; use all when rescheduling a meeting so participants receive updates.

notes: There are no transcript, recording, sharing or language options. To create an event without AI notes, use event-review; Google's defaults then apply. Edits, pasted meeting links and recurring events are refused.

If the meet-settings permission is missing, the review is refused here (MeetSettingsPermissionRequired), before any Calendar write. Google checks API enablement, plan and admin policy only when the setting is sent after the event is saved.
The Meet change names only the AI notes and transcription settings in its field mask, never a wildcard. Recording and all other Meet settings stay unchanged.

commands.summary: Confirm a reviewed operation exactly: create the event, then send the AI notes setting to its Meet link.
notes: Inspect state even when ok is true. applied: the event was created and Google's read-back shows AI notes and transcription on. partial: the event was saved but AI notes are not confirmed. rejected: Calendar refused the event and nothing was changed. unknown: the event save could not be confirmed. not_sent: no request reached Google. calendar.state is not_sent, applied, rejected or unknown. meetAiNotes.state is on, waiting_for_link, refused, unknown or not_sent.
on is a dated observation of Google's read-back, not a guarantee that the setting stays on. refused is final and does not show the current setting.

If meetAiNotes.state is waiting_for_link and meet-event-reconcile reports the link is ready, running meet-event-apply again with the same operation ID and review hash sends only the first Meet settings request. It never writes Calendar again. An unknown AI notes outcome is never resent.

commands.summary: Check a saved operation using Google reads only.
notes: Sends only Google GET requests and updates the local journal. It never writes Calendar, never changes Meet settings and never emails guests.
It reports the same states as meet-event-apply. on is reported only when Google's read-back matches both settings. Otherwise an unknown outcome stays unknown; this release has no retry.

commands.summary: Show the saved operation for a calendar or event without contacting Google.
notes: Reads the local journal only. Recorded states are what Omagma last observed, not Google's current settings.

CalendarId.description: Exact target.calendar_id returned by calendar.list for this explicit account, or "primary" for the account's primary calendar; replies report the actual calendar_id. Runtime bound: 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, no controls. Display names are not accepted.

CalendarMessageId.description: Provider mail message ID belonging to the explicit account; host resolves its original invitation bytes. Runtime bound: 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, no controls.

CalendarEventId.description: Exact provider event ID in the selected calendar. Runtime bound: 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, no controls.

CalendarOperationId.description: Stable reviewed operation ID. Reuse only for the same exact saved review; a different ID cannot bypass an unknown outcome for its identity.

CalendarReviewHash.description: Copy the exact lowercase SHA-256 reviewHash returned by calendar.review after inspecting the review. Example zeros are a placeholder, not a valid confirmation for an arbitrary review.

CalendarZone.description: IANA zone name such as Europe/Vienna or UTC. Runtime bound: 512 UTF-8 bytes; absolute paths and '..' are refused. No silent machine-zone fallback.

start.description: All-day YYYY-MM-DD, or local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS[.mmm]]. Offset-bearing RFC3339 is accepted if its offset matches timeZone.

end.description: Exclusive endpoint, later than start. An all-day single-date event ends on the following civil date.

attendees.description: Explicit guest emails; omit or null preserves all existing attendees and their RSVP metadata. New guests require sendUpdates all. Removing existing guests is not supported.

conference.description: none preserves an existing conference during edit; google_meet requests a unique Google Meet if calendar.supports_meet; link appends the provided joinUrl. Existing conference replacement is refused.

joinUrl.description: Safe HTTPS URL required only for conference link. Paste a meeting URL from any provider; Omagma does not create third-party conferences.

startOffset.description: Explicit UTC offset for an ambiguous local start, e.g. +02:00 or +01:00. Must match IANA rules for the selected instant.

endOffset.description: Explicit UTC offset for an ambiguous local end. Nonexistent local times are refused even with an offset.
